sources.citation: Venkataraman YR (2021). Ocean acidification influences on physiology and epigenetics in the Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas). PhD dissertation, University of Washington. Chapter 4: Polyploidy and environmental stress have distinct impacts on Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) ctenidia methylomes (pp. 86-112).
sources.read: full text of chapter 4 (abstract, methods, results, discussion, Table 4.1, Figs 4.1-4.4) and the Appendix A.4 data-accessibility list, from the ResearchWorks PDF

sources.citation: RobertsLab/project-oyster-oa GitHub repository, analyses/Haws_04-DSS/DML, Haws_07-DML-characterization, Haws_09-functional-enrichment (authors' own output cited in Appendix A.4).
sources.read: DSS DML tables (DML-pH-DSS.csv, DML-ploidy-DSS.csv, DML-ploidypH-DSS.csv) and enriched-GO-with-transcript tables; used only to make P1's claims precise (gene identities behind Table 4.1). NCBI Gene esummary used to resolve LOC gene IDs to product names.

caveats: These results come from run curious_mestorf, which aligned these non-directional (Zymo Pico Methyl-Seq) libraries in directional mode and so used about half of the read pairs (30% mapping). Calls are unbiased but at half depth; re-run with --non_directional (PR #61) and re-derive before treating the differential verdicts as final.

The paper is a dissertation chapter; the authors' own DML tables (RobertsLab/project-oyster-oa) label the pH and ploidy sets the other way round from the chapter's text. The claims follow the chapter.

claims.statement: Across all 24 samples, 11.6% of cytosines in CpG context were called methylated (Bismark, pooled over samples).
claims.re_derived: 10.94% (mean over 24 samples, all samples; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 11.6%

claims.statement: There was no global methylation difference between diploid and triploid oysters; both were predominantly lowly methylated (no difference value or test statistic reported).
claims.re_derived: ploidy diploid 10.81% vs triploid 11.07% (difference +0.26 points, permutation p = 0.142)
claims.rule: the paper reports no difference: p >= 0.05 replicated; inconclusive when the group sizes cannot reach p < 0.05

claims.statement: There were no global methylation differences between samples, including between low (7.7) and high (8.2) pH treatments (no values reported).
claims.re_derived: ph 7.7 10.90% vs 8.2 10.98% (difference +0.09 points, permutation p = 0.649)
claims.rule: the paper reports no difference: p >= 0.05 replicated; inconclusive when the group sizes cannot reach p < 0.05

claims.statement: A global PCA of CpG percent methylation (PC1 11.0%, PC2 6.63% of variance) did not separate samples by ploidy.
claims.re_derived: ploidy explains 4% (adjusted R^2) of PC1 (12.41% of variance); PCA of job main
claims.rule: the paper reports no separation: adjusted R^2 < 0.2 replicated; < 0.5 partly

claims.statement: The same global PCA did not separate samples by pH treatment.
claims.re_derived: ph explains 0% (adjusted R^2) of PC1 (12.41% of variance); PCA of job main
claims.rule: the paper reports no separation: adjusted R^2 < 0.2 replicated; < 0.5 partly

claims.statement: Of 10,497,320 CpGs with >=5x coverage in every sample, 9.4% were highly methylated (mean >=50%).
claims.re_derived: our tables are per gene, not per CpG

claims.statement: Methylation is concentrated in genes: 94.3% of highly methylated CpGs lay in genes (53.2% intronic, 35.7% CDS), a distribution significantly different from all 5x CpGs (chi-squared).
claims.re_derived: gene_body 14.73% vs genome 10.94% (CpG calls pooled over all genes, mean over samples)

claims.statement: Upstream 1 kb flanking regions held only 0.5% of highly methylated CpGs versus 94.3% in genes, implying low promoter-proximal methylation relative to gene bodies.
claims.re_derived: gene_body 14.73% vs promoter 3.66% (CpG calls pooled over all genes, mean over samples)

claims.statement: DSS multifactor model identified 154 ploidy-DML (ploidyT coefficient) out of 12,794,074 CpGs with >=1x coverage.
claims.re_derived: job main, ploidytriploid: gene_body: 7 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 1.03); promoter: 1 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.862); paper 154 DMCs
claims.rule: units differ (the paper counts DMCs, we count genes), so only presence is compared: both some partly, both none replicated, otherwise not replicated; approximate: our job pools over ph (paper: 8.2 only), so at most partly

claims.statement: DSS multifactor model identified 178 pH-DML (pHL coefficient).
claims.re_derived: job main, ph7.7: gene_body: 0 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 1.006); promoter: 3 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.883); paper 178 DMCs
claims.rule: units differ (the paper counts DMCs, we count genes), so only presence is compared: both some partly, both none replicated, otherwise not replicated; approximate: our job pools over ploidy (paper: diploid only), so at most partly

claims.statement: The ploidy x pH interaction term gave 53 interaction-DML.
claims.re_derived: Interaction contrast is not a registered contrast (registry has ploidy and ph main factors only); also CpG-level.

claims.statement: Ploidy-DML were mostly genic: 145 of 154 (94.2%) fell in 109 genes, chiefly introns (74.0%), then CDS (16.9%) and UTR (5.2%).
claims.re_derived: Counts genes containing a significant CpG, not genes tested as units; intron/CDS split also needs other regions.

claims.statement: pH-DML were mostly genic: 123 of 178 (69.1%) fell in 94 genes, chiefly introns (58.4%), with 48.3% in transposable elements and 15.2% intergenic.
claims.re_derived: Per-CpG locations in introns/TEs/intergenic are not available; genes-with-DML is not a per-gene test.

claims.statement: DML sets overlapped little: 21 loci shared by pH and ploidy, 11 by pH and interaction, 17 by ploidy and interaction, and 25 in all three.
claims.re_derived: Locus-level overlaps.

claims.statement: Chromosome 9 carried the most DML per 10,000 CpGs despite having the fewest genes.
claims.re_derived: Per-chromosome DML density on the Roslin assembly.

claims.statement: Few DML overlapped C/T SNPs (5 pH-DML, 3 ploidy-DML, 1 interaction-DML), so DML were not SNP artefacts.
claims.re_derived: Locus-level SNP overlap.

claims.statement: Genes with ploidy-DML were enriched for protein dephosphorylation and cell-cell adhesion (3 BP terms, 2 genes each); the dephosphorylation gene carries 3 ploidy-DML.
claims.re_derived: job main, ploidytriploid: 0 replicated, 0 partly, 1 not, of 1 tested (0 not found in the annotation, 0 not tested)
claims.rule: per gene: FDR < 0.05 in the claimed direction replicated, p < 0.05 partly (both corrected for the number of matching genes and regions); claim: most tested genes replicated, any replicated or partly: partly; approximate: our job pools over ph (paper: 8.2 only), so at most partly

claims.statement: Interaction-DML genes showed no significantly enriched GO terms, so ploidy and pH together showed no clear functional signature.
claims.re_derived: Interaction contrast not registered; GO enrichment not part of re-derived results.

claims.statement: Functions of ploidy-DML genes do not resemble those reported for naturally polyploid organisms (e.g. transposon silencing, transcriptional control).
claims.re_derived: Interpretive comparison with other taxa.

claims.statement: Both ploidy- and pH-DML were enriched in genes with multiple transcripts, suggesting regulation via alternative splicing.
claims.re_derived: Transcript-structure/splicing inference; no RNA-seq.

claims.statement: Pairwise Pearson correlations of CpG methylation between samples were uniformly high (0.87-0.93).
claims.re_derived: Computed on per-CpG methylKit profiles (>=5x, >=8 samples per group).

claims.statement: Coverage was similarly distributed in diploids and triploids (of 12.79 M CpGs with >=1x, 5.40 M had higher mean coverage in triploids).
claims.re_derived: Per-CpG coverage comparison; per-library CpGs covered is available but the claim is about the coverage distribution.

claims.statement: 61.0% of trimmed read pairs aligned uniquely to the Roslin genome plus mitochondrion (7.4 x 10^8 of ~2.4 x 10^9 reads).
claims.re_derived: Alignment metric on a different genome assembly and aligner settings (non-directional, score_min L,0,-0.6).
